terms.meaning: The outermost solid layer of the Earth ("litho" means rock), thick under continents and thin under the sea.
Molten rock is magma while underground, and lava once it comes out.
Vent: passage for magma. Crater: funnel-shaped hollow on top. Caldera: large basin-shaped crater with steep sides.
Focus: where an earthquake starts inside the crust. Epicentre: the point on the surface straight above it.
The study of earthquakes. A Seismograph records the waves.
A large sea wave caused by an underwater earthquake. The Japanese word means harbour waves.
The breaking down of rocks by temperature, rain, wind and other agents.
Changing the land's surface by rivers, glaciers, groundwater, wind and sea waves.
A porous rock bed that holds a lot of underground water.

items.name: Age and heat of the Earth
items.formula: More than 4.6 billion years old.
items.example: Going down, it gets 1°C hotter every 32 metres, so we have reached only 10 to 12 km.

items.name: The Crust
items.formula: Top layer, about 60 km deep. Upper part SIAL (silica, aluminium): continental. Lower part SIMA (silica, magnesium): oceanic.
items.example: Lighter materials are on top.

items.name: The Mantle
items.formula: Middle layer, down to 2900 km, with semi-molten magma.
items.example: The Moho separates crust and mantle; Gutenberg separates mantle and core.

items.name: The Core
items.formula: Innermost layer, down to 6371 km, called NIFE (nickel and iron).
items.example: The outer core is molten and the inner core is solid.

items.name: Igneous (primary) rocks
items.formula: Formed by cooling of molten matter; the first rocks.
items.example: "Igneous" comes from Latin Ignis and Sanskrit Agni, meaning fire.

items.name: Intrusive and extrusive igneous rocks
items.formula: Intrusive: cool slowly underground, large crystals (granite). Extrusive: cool fast on the surface, fine or glassy (basalt).
items.example: Same magma, but where it cools changes the crystals.

items.name: Sedimentary (secondary) rocks
items.formula: Broken pieces carried by water, wind or ice, laid down in layers.
items.example: Also called stratified or aqueous rocks.

items.name: Three kinds of sedimentary rock
items.formula: Mechanical: sandstone, shale. Chemical: rock salt, gypsum. Organic: limestone, coal.
items.example: Rock salt forms when salty water evaporates.

items.name: Metamorphic rocks and what they come from
items.formula: Heat and pressure change old rock. Granite → Gneiss, Basalt → Schist, Limestone → Marble.
items.example: Also Sandstone → Quartzite and Coal → Graphite → Diamond. They are the hardest rocks.

items.name: Types of volcano
items.formula: Active: Stromboli, Etna. Dormant: Vesuvius, Fujiyama, Kilimanjaro. Extinct: Aconcagua, Arthur's Seat.
items.example: There are about 1350 active volcanoes in the world.

items.name: Pacific Ring of Fire
items.formula: The Circum-Pacific Belt, around the Pacific's edges, with the largest volcanoes.
items.example: Others: the Mid-Atlantic Belt and the Mid-Continental Belt.

items.name: Causes of earthquakes
items.formula: Moving plates, volcanoes, faulting and human actions such as big dams and mines.
items.example: Koyna dam in Maharashtra is the book's human-made example.

items.name: Three earthquake waves
items.formula: Primary: fastest, pass through all matter. Secondary: can't pass through liquids. Surface: slowest but most destructive.
items.example: The Richter scale records magnitude.

items.name: Three types of weathering
items.formula: Mechanical: broken with no chemical change. Chemical: rainwater changes the minerals. Biological: plants, animals and people.
items.example: Chemical types: oxidation, carbonation, hydration, solution.

items.name: A river's three courses
items.formula: Upper: erosion, V valleys, waterfalls. Middle: carrying, meanders. Lower: deposits, flood plains, deltas.
items.example: The river's work is the Fluvial Cycle.

items.name: Parts of a river system
items.formula: Source: where it begins. Mouth: where it meets the sea. Tributary: a stream feeding it. Confluence: where they join.
items.example: An estuary is a tidal mouth; a delta is a fan of deposits.

items.name: Work of a glacier
items.formula: Slow-moving ice. Erosion: cirque, horn, U valleys. Deposits: moraines.
items.example: Moraines are lateral, medial, ground and terminal. The work is the Glacial Cycle.

items.name: Springs, geysers and artesian wells
items.formula: Perennial: always flowing. Intermittent: sometimes. Hot: warm water. Geyser: a jet (Old Faithful, USA).
items.example: Artesian wells, common in Australia, come from a basin between non-porous rocks.

items.name: Karst topography
items.formula: Limestone landforms made by underground water: sinkholes, caves, stalactites and stalagmites.
items.example: Limestone caves in India: Akalagavi (Ulavi), Belum and Bohra.

items.name: Work of wind and sea waves
items.formula: Wind (Aeolian cycle): mushroom rocks, barchans, loess. Waves: cliffs, sea caves, stacks, beaches.
items.example: The Loess plain of China is yellow soil.

mistakes.text: It is magma underground and lava only after it reaches the surface.
Stalactites hang from the roof; stalagmites rise from the floor.
The focus is underground. The epicentre is on the surface above it.
Primary waves are fastest, but the slowest surface waves do the most damage.
